record.paper_title: Developments and open problems on chiral polytopes
record.original_question: For regular or enantiomorphic forms of chiral polytopes K1 and K2, not both regular, determine the automorphism group of the universal chiral amalgamation {K1, K2}_ch and give conditions under which this universal amalgamation is finite.

evidence.quote: Problem 32 Determine the group of the universal amalgamation {K1, K2}ch and give conditions under which this is finite, where K1 and K2 are regular or enantiomorphic forms of chiral polytopes, not both regular.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An abstract polytope of rank $n$ is a partially ordered set $P$ (whose elements are called faces) satisfying the standard axioms for abstract polytopes: $P$ has a unique minimum face and unique maximum face; every maximal chain (flag) has length $n+1$; $P$ is strongly flag-connected; and $P$ satisfies the diamond condition (for any faces $F<G$ with $\mathrm{rank}(G)-\mathrm{rank}(F)=2$, there are exactly two faces strictly between $F$ and $G$). The automorphism group $\Gamma(P)$ consists of order-preserving bijections of $P$ to itself.

A polytope $P$ of rank $n$ is regular if $\Gamma(P)$ acts transitively on the flags of $P$. It is chiral if $\Gamma(P)$ has exactly two orbits on the flags such that adjacent flags lie in different orbits. A chiral polytope $P$ comes in an enantiomorphic pair: $P$ and its mirror image $P^*$ are isomorphic as polytopes only as unoriented structures, and one calls $P$ and $P^*$ the two enantiomorphic forms.

Given two abstract polytopes $K_1$ of rank $n$ and $K_2$ of rank $n$ such that the vertex figure of $K_2$ is isomorphic to the facet of a rank-$(n+1)$ structure whose facets are isomorphic to $K_1$ (equivalently: $K_1$ and $K_2$ are compatible facet/vertex-figure data), and assuming each of $K_1$, $K_2$ is either regular or chiral (with a chosen enantiomorphic form) but not both regular, the universal chiral amalgamation $\{K_1, K_2\}_{\mathrm{ch}}$ is defined as the universal chiral polytope of rank $n+1$ whose facets are isomorphic to $K_1$ and whose vertex figures are isomorphic to $K_2$, characterized by the property that every chiral polytope with this facet and vertex-figure data is a quotient of $\{K_1, K_2\}_{\mathrm{ch}}$.

Problem. Determine the automorphism group $\Gamma(\{K_1, K_2\}_{\mathrm{ch}})$ of the universal chiral amalgamation $\{K_1, K_2\}_{\mathrm{ch}}$, and provide necessary and sufficient conditions on $K_1$ and $K_2$ for $\{K_1, K_2\}_{\mathrm{ch}}$ to be finite.
artifact.status_search_result: No specific resolution of this problem appears in the literature. Related work (Cunningham–Pellicer on chiral extensions, Schulte–Weiss surveys, free extensions of chiral polytopes) treats special cases and existence of chiral extensions, but a general determination of the automorphism group of the universal chiral amalgamation and finiteness criteria for mixed regular/chiral facet–vertex-figure pairs has not been completed. The problem appears to remain open in general.

status_evidence.title: Chiral extensions of chiral polytopes
status_evidence.snippet: Among all chiral polytopes with given facets there is a universal such polytope whose group is a certain amalgamated product of the groups involved.
status_evidence.claim: Universal chiral amalgamations are studied but no general determination of their automorphism groups or finiteness criteria has been given.

status_evidence.title: Free Extensions of Chiral Polytopes
status_evidence.snippet: Constructions of universal/free chiral extensions; finiteness analysis only in special cases.
